title: I built a 60 FPS physics arcade game in Jetpack Compose using AI as my Lead Architect — Lessons from fixing game-feel, retention & procedural modes
author: YakFederal3939
selftext:
Hey everyone! 👋

I wanted to share a breakdown of \*\*Orbit Jumper\*\*, an arcade orbital physics game built natively on Android using \*\*Kotlin & Jetpack Compose\*\*, where AI served as a continuous pair-programmer, math optimizer, and systems designer throughout the lifecycle of the project.

\### 🎮 What is Orbit Jumper?

The core loop revolves around gravity assists: your starship orbits celestial bodies, and you tap to slingshot between orbits while calculating launch tangents, dodging orbital asteroid belts, and surviving dynamic cosmic weather anomalies. 

We recently rolled out two major gameplay systems:

1. \*\*The Gravity Whip (Mid-Flight Vector Steering):\*\* Instead of static flight arcs, players can burn ion thrusters mid-flight to dynamically curve their trajectory toward nearby gravitational wells, rewarding clutch saves with combo points.

2. \*\*Supernova Rush Mode:\*\* A high-octane survival mode where an animated solar plasma wall chases you from below and planets suffer thermal overload if you linger longer than 2.8s. Quick-jumping knocks the fire wall back.

\---

\### 🤖 Where AI Actually Moved the Needle:

1. \*\*Deterministic Physics without Game Engines:\*\*

   Instead of Unity or Godot, the entire game runs directly on Android Canvas with a custom fixed-step accumulator (60Hz tick loop) for 120Hz/144Hz display sync. We used AI to generate pre-computed sine/cosine lookup tables (\`StellarMathOptimizer\`) and optimize draw passes to maintain steady 60+ FPS with zero garbage collection spikes during rendering.

2. \*\*Diagnosing the "Leaky Bucket" (Product Analytics):\*\*

   When our D1 retention dipped, we fed session data and Android Vitals into the AI to analyze rage-quits. The AI helped pinpoint that early cadence curves were too unforgiving. We implemented dynamic "Coyote Gravity" wells and early capture assist radii for novice stages that immediately lowered early churn.

3. \*\*Ad-Mediation & Architectural Fixes:\*\*

   Frequent Compose recompositions were recreating AdMob banner views and triggering duplicate preload requests, tanking our match rates. AI helped architect a singleton caching pattern in Compose interoperability, eliminating ghost calls and stabilizing ad performance.

4. \*\*Multiplayer Emulation & Rival Bots:\*\*

   For our asynchronous PvP mode (\*Cosmic Rush\*), AI designed the rival ghost telemetry and collision response physics so opponents crash realistically into boundary walls and asteroids with full particle feedback instead of disappearing artificially.

\---

\### 💡 Biggest Takeaways

\* \*\*AI excels at discrete math and state machines in codebases you fully control.\*\* Generating orbital tangencies, deflection matrices, and procedural wave algorithms saved days of trial and error.

\* \*\*Game Feel Still Needs Human Taste.\*\* AI can give you the vector math for a gravity whip, but tweaking the springiness, screen-shake duration, and haptic rumble to make it feel visceral requires hands-on iteration.

\---

\### 🔗 Try it out & Feedback:

If you want to check out the physics feel, APK, or share thoughts on the mechanics:

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.aistudio.orbitjumper.hpsqkx

I'd love to hear how other devs here are balancing pure code-driven arcade gameplay vs. full engines when working with AI assistance!
